intro: Pattaya is a serious buffet town. You'll find everything from beachfront seafood BBQ for a few hundred baht right up to beachside hotel buffets with lobster, imported oysters, and sashimi all in one sitting. We've picked 11 spots that Pattaya locals and frequent visitors actually talk about, split into three clear groups: hotel buffets, beachfront seafood BBQ, and in-town mookata and shabu. For each one we note the area, a rough price, and which dishes are worth going for.
chips: 💸 From a few hundred baht to all-out

blocks.html: Before the ranking, here's the honest breakdown: Pattaya buffets fall into roughly three types, and the prices are clearly different. First, hotel buffets (usually several hundred baht up to four figures, with wide food lines, good seafood, and a nice setting). Second, beachfront seafood BBQ buffets (mid-hundreds, with grilled seafood, shellfish, and prawns plus a view). And third, mookata, shabu, and yakiniku in town (the cheapest, great for eating in a big group). The prices listed are rough per-person ranges — these swing with weekday vs. weekend and each month's promotion, so leave a little wiggle room and check the latest price with the restaurant before you go to be safe.

blocks.text: 11 Pattaya buffets people actually go to

items.name: Jimmy BBQ & Grill — Grand Palazzo Hotel
items.blurb: A popular hotel buffet in Central Pattaya with a wide spread: sashimi, sushi, grilled seafood, barbecue, pasta, pizza, Thai dishes, and a chocolate-fondue dessert corner. The hotel reviews sit around 8.5/10, with guests praising the variety and value. It often runs in seatings, so book ahead and ask about that month's promo before you go.
items.meta: Central Pattaya · hotel buffet · often in seatings

items.name: Seafood Buffet — Mövenpick Siam Na Jomtien
items.blurb: The seafood buffet at this beachfront hotel on Na Jomtien beach. The draw is the sheer amount of seafood — grilled tiger prawns, mantis shrimp, steamed blue swimmer crab, imported oysters, river prawns, New Zealand mussels, and salmon and tuna sashimi. It suits a special meal or a celebration where you want to go all-out on seafood by the sea. It costs more than the other groups, so check the open days and price ahead.
items.meta: Na Jomtien · beachfront hotel buffet · special occasion

items.name: Seafood Buffet — Holiday Inn Pattaya
items.blurb: A seafood-themed buffet on a high floor of this beachfront Pattaya hotel, with a full view of Pattaya Bay. It usually runs only on certain days of the week (around Thursday–Saturday), focused on seafood and international lines. Good for couples or families who want both the view and the seafood. Prices start in the four figures and don't include drinks, so book a window table ahead.
items.meta: North Pattaya · beachfront · high-floor sea view · select days

items.name: International Buffet — OZO North Pattaya
items.blurb: A poolside buffet in North Pattaya that people talk up for value: pay a little over five hundred baht and you can stay for several hours, with menus that rotate so they don't repeat day to day. The international lines are varied, making it a good fit for anyone who wants a hotel setting without blowing the budget. Prices and promos change by season, so check before you go.
items.meta: North Pattaya · poolside hotel buffet · daily-rotating menu
tags: Linger as long as you like

items.name: Waves & Wind Buffet — Grand Centre Point Pattaya
items.blurb: An international dinner buffet at this hotel in the middle of Pattaya. The draw is a price in the seven-hundreds for a wide spread across Thai, Japanese, and Western dishes. It has run on select days (such as every Saturday) as all-you-can-eat with no time limit. Good for anyone who wants a hotel buffet in town that's easy to reach — check the open days and seatings before booking.
items.meta: Central Pattaya · in-town hotel buffet · select days

items.name: Sut Khet Talay Phao (Jomtien)
items.blurb: A grilled-seafood BBQ buffet right by the water in the Jomtien area, in the few-hundred-baht group: grilled seafood, mookata, snacks, and a sushi corner. The draw is the beachfront setting paired with the value, and it's great for coming with a group on a budget. It gets crowded on weekends, so arrive in the early evening to grab a view table more easily.

items.name: Amporn Seafood Buffet (Pattaya Sai 3)
items.blurb: A go-for-it seafood buffet that fans love for the sheer amount of seafood — prawns, mantis shrimp, shellfish, crab, plus snacks. Priced in the hundreds, it's about volume and satisfaction rather than a fancy setting. Good for anyone who wants to demolish unlimited seafood on a light budget. The popular items run out fast at peak times, so go early to get the full spread.

items.name: Ninja Mookata & Talay Phao (North Pattaya)
items.blurb: A spot in North Pattaya that combines grilled-seafood BBQ with mookata under one roof, with a varied menu and plenty of snacks. Prices are friendly, making it a good fit for families or groups of friends who want both the grill and the dipping. It's not about the view — it's about a filling, good-value meal.

items.name: Umami Chill Buffet (Khao Talo)
items.blurb: A buffet in the Khao Talo area that gives you everything under one roof — mookata, butter grill, jim jum hot pot, and a seafood corner. Good for groups of friends who like several styles in one meal. Priced in the hundreds, locals go for the value and the wide choice. There's parking, so it's easy to come as a group.
items.meta: Khao Talo, Pattaya City · mookata–jim jum–seafood

items.name: Fuku Yakiniku (Sukhumvit–Pattaya)
items.blurb: A Japanese-style yakiniku buffet in the Sukhumvit–Pattaya area. The draw is the meat — including wagyu-grade beef — plus river prawns, sashimi, and sushi on the line. It costs more than a typical mookata but you get the meat quality, making it a fit for anyone serious about grilling beef Japanese-style. Check the packages and price before you go.

items.name: AA Mookata (Central Pattaya–Map Prachan)
items.blurb: The lightest-priced mookata on the list — pay just over a hundred baht and you're full. The menu has plenty of choice in classic neighborhood-mookata style, making it a fit for tight budgets, students, or groups of friends who just want to sit, grill, and chat for hours. Nothing fancy, but filling and good value.

blocks.title: How to read buffet prices
blocks.html: The hotel-buffet price you see usually doesn't include the service charge and VAT — some places add around 17% at the bill — and it usually doesn't include drinks either. For the few-hundred-baht BBQ buffets, also check whether there's a "leftover charge": if you take food and don't finish it, some places add a fee by weight. Ask clearly before you start so there are no surprises when you pay.

blocks.text: Which buffet to pick for your trip

items.name: Want all-out seafood — a celebration meal
items.blurb: Go for a beachfront hotel buffet like Mövenpick or Holiday Inn — lobster, imported oysters, sashimi, and a sea view, in exchange for a four-figure price. Best for a special day.

items.name: Want the hotel setting without blowing the budget
items.blurb: OZO North or Waves & Wind at Grand Centre Point, priced in the five- to seven-hundreds, with wide international lines, in town, and easy to reach — good value for a mid-range budget.

items.name: Want a relaxed, easy-on-the-wallet meal
items.blurb: Beachfront grilled-seafood BBQ at Jomtien, or mookata–yakiniku in town, in the low-to-mid hundreds. Great for coming with a big group and sitting around for a long, chatty meal.

blocks.text: Dishes to grab first at a Pattaya buffet

blocks.html: A buffet pays off most when you go straight for the items that are pricey to buy on their own. Here's what Pattaya locals say to grab first in each type.

items: Oysters / tiger prawns / mantis shrimp — at hotel buffets, these are the priciest to buy separately, so grab them early while the line is still full.
Salmon and tuna sashimi — the corner that runs out fastest at hotel buffets. Go early for thick, fresh cuts.
Grilled seafood, prawns, and cockles — at beachfront BBQ buffets, this is the star that makes the per-head price worth it. Grill it just to done and don't leave it sitting.
Japanese-style beef — at yakiniku spots, grab the premium cuts first, since they often come out in batches and run out quickly.
Snacks and fried items — take these later, since they're topped up constantly and are cheap to buy on their own. Don't fill up on them before the expensive stuff.

blocks.text: Enjoying Pattaya safely around your buffet meal

blocks.title: A friendly heads-up
blocks.html: Pattaya has nightlife areas like Walking Street. If you're heading out after your buffet, party with a clear head, keep an eye on your wallet and valuables, and don't hand things to or drink with strangers. If you're planning a boat trip to Koh Larn the next day, always check the weather and sea conditions first — the sea on this side changes fast in the rainy season. Room and tour prices also swing with the season and holidays, so compare a few options before booking to get a better rate.

blocks.text: Tips for eating Pattaya buffets well — and not getting surprised by the bill

items: Check the month's price and promo before you go — hotel buffets change promos often, and some months have big discounts. The restaurant's page or a quick call gets you the real price.
Ask about service charge + VAT — many hotels add around 17% at the bill, so budget for it and you won't get a shock.
Book a seating and a view table — hotel buffets often run in seatings and the seaside tables fill fast; on weekends, book ahead.
Go in the early evening — for both hotel buffets and beachfront BBQ, the lines are still full and the seafood is still all there. Come late and the good stuff is often gone.
Check the leftover rules — some BBQ buffets charge a leftover fee by weight, so take bite-sized portions and refill later to stay good value and avoid the penalty.

faq.q: How much does a Pattaya hotel buffet cost?
faq.a: Most run around ฿600–1,500 per person, depending on whether it's a general international buffet or an all-out seafood theme. For example, OZO North and Waves & Wind at Grand Centre Point sit in the five- to seven-hundreds, while beachfront seafood spots like Mövenpick and Holiday Inn run into the four figures. Prices usually don't include the roughly 17% service charge and VAT, and they change with each month's promo, so check before you go to be safe.

faq.q: Where should I go for an all-out Pattaya seafood buffet?
faq.a: If you want unlimited lobster, imported oysters, mantis shrimp, steamed blue swimmer crab, and sashimi, the seafood buffets at beachfront hotels like Mövenpick Siam Na Jomtien and the seafood theme at Holiday Inn Pattaya are the ones people talk about. They run into the four figures but you get a packed seafood spread and a sea view, ideal for a special meal. Book ahead and check the seafood-theme open days.

faq.q: Are there Pattaya buffets that are cheap but filling and good value?
faq.a: Yes — go for beachfront grilled-seafood BBQ at Jomtien, or mookata–yakiniku in town, priced in the low-to-mid hundreds. For example, Sut Khet Talay Phao, Umami Chill, or AA Mookata starting around ฿159 will fill you up and let you sit around with friends comfortably. Great for a tight budget.

faq.q: Do I need to book a Pattaya hotel buffet ahead?
faq.a: We'd recommend it, especially on weekends, since many hotel buffets run in timed seatings and the seaside tables fill fast. On top of that, some themes — like the Holiday Inn seafood night — run only on certain days of the week. Calling to book and asking about seatings, prices, and promos ahead helps you avoid a wasted trip.

faq.q: When is the best value time to eat a Pattaya buffet?
faq.a: The early evening is a good time, since the food lines are still full and the seafood and sashimi are all still there. The items that are pricey to buy separately — oysters, tiger prawns, and sashimi — tend to run out fast on busy days. Grab the expensive stuff first, then follow up with the snacks that get topped up constantly, and you'll get the most for your per-head price.
